relations.definition: To select or choose someone or something for a particular award or recognition.
relations.embedding_query_text: nominates: To select or choose someone or something for a particular award or recognition.

instances: Primetime Emmy Awards -> Margo's Got Money Troubles

chosen_property.label: nominates
chosen_property.definition: To select or choose someone or something for a particular award or recognition.
chosen_property.justification: No existing property fits the relation.

candidates.label: awards
candidates.comment: Awards won by or for a creative work, organization, person, or product. Also called: honors, prizes, recognitions. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' awards 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' awards 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' awards 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from award, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: award
candidates.comment: An award won by or for a creative work, organization, person, product, or service. Also called: honor, prize, recognition. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' award 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' award 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' award 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from awards, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: candidate
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a vote action, indicating the person who is being voted for. Also called "voted for", "nominee", "electoral candidate". Examples: "Election vote action candidate Jane Smith", "Award vote action candidate John Doe".

candidates.label: option
candidates.comment: A text or thing representing an option available for a choose action. Also called choice, alternative, selection. Examples: "Choose Meal Action option 'Chicken'", "Choose Color Action option 'Blue'", "Choose Destination Action option 'Paris'". Distinct from object, which is the general item acted upon.

candidates.label: recognizedBy
candidates.comment: A recognition relation between a credential and the organization that acknowledges its validity or value. Also called accredited by, validated by, acknowledged by. Examples: "A university degree is recognized by 'the Ministry of Education'.", "A professional certification is recognized by 'an industry association'.", "A medical license is recognized by 'the Medical Board'."

candidates.label: recognizingAuthority
candidates.comment: A recognizing authority relation between a medical entity and the organization that officially endorses it within a system of medicine. Also called endorsed by, officially recognized by. Examples: "A medical treatment is recognized by 'the World Health Organization'.", "A medical specialty is recognized by 'the American Medical Association'.", "A traditional medicine practice is recognized by 'a national health ministry'."

candidates.label: credentialCategory
candidates.comment: A classification relation between a credential and its type or category. Also called: credential type, certification category, award type. Examples: "PhD" credential category "degree", "PMP" credential category "certificate", "Scout Badge" credential category "badge", "Driver's License" credential category "license".

candidates.label: name
candidates.comment: A name or title identifying a thing. Also called title, designation, appellation, label. Examples: "Book name 'The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy'", "Person name 'Alice Smith'", "Company name 'Acme Corp'". Distinct from alternateName, which is an alias or alternative name.

candidates.label: educationalCredentialAwarded
candidates.comment: An educational credential awarded relation between a course or program and the credential received upon successful completion. Also called "award received", "qualification granted", "certificate earned". Examples: "Course 'Introduction to Python' educationalCredentialAwarded 'Certificate of Completion'", "Program 'MBA' educationalCredentialAwarded 'Master of Business Administration'", "Training 'First Aid' educationalCredentialAwarded 'First Aid Certification'".

candidates.label: winner
candidates.comment: A winner relation between a losing action and the person who won it. Also called victor, triumphant participant, successful party. Examples: ChessMatchLoseAction winner Alice, RaceLoseAction winner Bob, CompetitionLoseAction winner Charlie.

relations.definition: To appear or perform in a movie, TV show, or other production.
relations.embedding_query_text: starsIn: To appear or perform in a movie, TV show, or other production.

instances: Matthew Rhys -> The Beast in Me
Claire Danes -> The Beast in Me

chosen_property.label: actor
chosen_property.justification: Flipped to inverse to match the subject-object direction.

candidates.label: actors
candidates.comment: An actor relation between a creative work (e.g., movie, episode, video game) and a person who performs in it. Also called performer, cast member, player. Examples: "A movie's actors include 'Brad Pitt'.", "An episode's actors include 'Jennifer Aniston'." Distinct from actor, which is the preferred and more general property that also allows PerformingGroup.

candidates.label: actor
candidates.comment: An actor relation between a creative work (e.g., movie, episode, video game) or event and a person or performing group who performs in it. Also called performer, cast member, player. Examples: "A movie's actor is 'Tom Hanks'.", "A play's actor is 'The Ensemble Theatre'.", "An episode's actor is 'Jane Doe'." Distinct from actors, which is a deprecated property for the same concept.

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.

candidates.label: titleEIDR
candidates.comment: An EIDR title relation between a movie, TV episode, season, or series and its Entertainment Identifier Registry (EIDR) identifier at the work level. Also called EIDR work ID, entertainment ID, film/TV EIDR. Examples: "Movie titleEIDR '10.5240/7EC7-228A-510A-053E-CBB8-J'", "TV series titleEIDR '10.5240/B123-C456-D789-E012-F345-G'", "TVEpisode titleEIDR '10.5240/A1B2-C3D4-E5F6-G7H8-I9J0-K'". Distinct from editEIDR, which identifies a specific variant or expression of a work.

candidates.label: performers
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and its primary performers, who can be organizations or persons. Also called main artists, headliners, principal actors, featured performers. Examples: A concert has performers 'Coldplay'. A play has performers 'The Royal Shakespeare Company'. A festival has performers 'Various Artists'. Distinct from performer, which can be any performer, not necessarily the main one.

candidates.label: character
candidates.comment: A fictional role relation between a creative work and a person who is a character within it. Also called "fictional person", "role played by", "depicted character". Examples: "Novel 'Pride and Prejudice' character Elizabeth Bennet", "Movie 'Star Wars' character Luke Skywalker".

candidates.label: subtitleLanguage
candidates.comment: An identification of the languages in which subtitles or captions are available for a broadcast event, movie, or TV episode. Also called "caption language", "available subtitles", "subtitle options". Examples: "The movie has subtitleLanguage English", "The TV episode's subtitleLanguage is Spanish", "This broadcast event offers subtitles in multiple subtitleLanguage options."

candidates.label: workPresented
candidates.comment: A presented work relation between a screening event and a movie, identifying the film shown during that event. Also called screened movie, film shown, featured film. Examples: ScreeningEvent workPresented "The Matrix", FilmFestivalEvent workPresented "Parasite", DriveInMovie workPresented "Jaws". Distinct from workFeatured, which is a general showcasing, and workPerformed, which is for live enactments.

candidates.label: entertainmentBusiness
candidates.comment: An entertainment business relation between a perform action and the entertainment business where the action occurred. Also called "venue", "performance location", "showplace". Examples: "Perform action entertainmentBusiness 'Concert Hall'", "Perform action entertainmentBusiness 'Theater Royal'", "Perform action entertainmentBusiness 'Comedy Club'". Distinct from location, which is a more general property for any place an action occurs.

relations.definition: To include or contain something as a part of a larger whole.
relations.embedding_query_text: involves: To include or contain something as a part of a larger whole.

instances: Emmy Award Nominations -> Primetime Emmy Awards

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: includedComposition
candidates.comment: A composition inclusion relation between a music composition and a smaller music composition that is part of it. Also called part of composition, contains composition, movement of. Examples: "A symphony has an included composition as a movement.", "A musical work includes a composition.", "This composition contains several included compositions.". Distinct from hasPart, which is a general part-whole relation for creative works.

candidates.label: hasBioChemEntityPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a biochemical entity and one of its constituent biochemical entities. Also called composed of, contains, includes part, made of. Examples: "A protein has a BioChemEntity part of an amino acid sequence.", "A cell has BioChemEntity parts like organelles.", "A molecule has BioChemEntity parts of atoms."

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: containedIn
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedIn 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedIn 'Paris'". Distinct from containedInPlace, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: containsPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and another smaller place that it contains. Also called "includes place", "encompasses", "holds". Examples: "Country 'France' containsPlace 'Paris'", "City 'Paris' containsPlace 'Eiffel Tower'". Distinct from containedIn or containedInPlace, which are the inverse relations.

candidates.label: containedInPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedInPlace 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedInPlace 'Paris'". Distinct from containedIn, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: includesObject
candidates.comment: A composition relation between an offer or product collection and the specific products and their quantities it contains. Also called composed of, contains, comprises, consists of, has as object. Examples: An offer includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 2 apples. A product collection includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 5 books. A demand includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 1 car.

candidates.label: superEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a smaller event and the larger event of which it is a part. Also called "part of larger event", "parent event", "contained within event", "main event". Examples: "The concert has superEvent the music festival", "The presentation's superEvent is the conference", "This workshop is part of a superEvent summit.". Distinct from subEvent, which points from the larger event to the smaller one.

candidates.label: isPartOfBioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A biochemical part-whole relation indicating that one biochemical entity is a component of another larger biochemical entity. Also called component of biochem entity, contained within biochem entity, element of biochem entity. Examples: A protein domain isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a larger protein'. A subunit isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a protein complex'. A specific gene sequence isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a chromosome'.

relations.definition: To declare or make known something officially or publicly.
relations.embedding_query_text: announces: To declare or make known something officially or publicly.

chosen_property.label: announces
chosen_property.definition: To declare or make known publicly.
chosen_property.justification: No existing property fits the relation.

candidates.label: announcementLocation
candidates.comment: An announcement location relation between a special announcement and the specific civic structure or local business it pertains to. Also called relevant location, associated place, specific venue. Examples: "A special announcement's announcement location is 'City Hall'.", "The emergency announcement's announcement location is 'Local Grocery Store'." Distinct from spatialCoverage, which is used for larger geographic regions.

candidates.label: releaseDate
candidates.comment: A release date relation between a product and the date it was made available to the public. Also called launch date, availability date, publication date. Examples: "A new smartphone model has a release date of 2024-03-01.", "A software update has a release date of 2023-11-15.", "A new car model has a release date of 2025-01-01.". Distinct from productionDate, which is when the item was manufactured.

candidates.label: recognizingAuthority
candidates.comment: A recognizing authority relation between a medical entity and the organization that officially endorses it within a system of medicine. Also called endorsed by, officially recognized by. Examples: "A medical treatment is recognized by 'the World Health Organization'.", "A medical specialty is recognized by 'the American Medical Association'.", "A traditional medicine practice is recognized by 'a national health ministry'."

candidates.label: legalName
candidates.comment: An official identification relation between an organization and its formally registered name. Also called registered name, official company name, corporate name, full legal name. Examples: An organization has a legalName of 'Acme Corporation Inc.'. A company's legalName is 'Global Solutions LLC'. The charity's legalName is 'Helping Hands Foundation'. Distinct from name, which is the common or display name.

candidates.label: publicAccess
candidates.comment: A public access relation indicating whether a place is open to public visitors. Also called open to public, publicly accessible. Examples: "A park has public access 'true'.", "A private residence has public access 'false'.", "A museum has public access 'true'."

candidates.label: diseasePreventionInfo
candidates.comment: A disease prevention information relation between a special announcement and a URL or web content providing details about disease prevention. Also called "prevention guidelines", "health advice". Examples: "Special announcement diseasePreventionInfo 'cdc.gov/prevention'", "Public health alert diseasePreventionInfo 'WebContent on handwashing'", "COVID-19 update diseasePreventionInfo 'who.int/prevention'".

candidates.label: copyrightNotice
candidates.comment: A textual declaration relation between a creative work and the statement describing its copyright aspects. Also called: copyright statement, copyright declaration, copyright text. Examples: "My Novel" copyright notice "© 2023 John Doe", "Company Website" copyright notice "Copyright 2023 Example Corp. All Rights Reserved.", "Academic Paper" copyright notice "Published under CC BY 4.0 license". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which identifies the entity owning the copyright.

candidates.label: publicTransportClosuresInfo
candidates.comment: A public transport closures information relation between a special announcement and details regarding public transport disruptions. Also called transport closure details, public transit alerts. Examples: "A special announcement includes public transport closures info about subway lines.", "An emergency alert provides public transport closures info for bus routes.", "A news update contains public transport closures info for train services."

candidates.label: quarantineGuidelines
candidates.comment: A quarantine guidelines relation between a special announcement and information regarding quarantine rules. Also called isolation rules, self-quarantine instructions. Examples: "A special announcement provides quarantine guidelines for travelers.", "A public health update includes quarantine guidelines for close contacts.", "A government notice details quarantine guidelines for returning citizens."

candidates.label: diseaseSpreadStatistics
candidates.comment: A disease spread statistics relation between a special announcement and a dataset, observation, URL, or web content containing statistical information about the spread of a disease. Also called "epidemic data", "infection rates", "case statistics". Examples: "Special announcement diseaseSpreadStatistics 'Dataset of daily cases'", "Public health update diseaseSpreadStatistics 'WebContent on regional spread'", "COVID-19 alert diseaseSpreadStatistics 'URL to dashboard'".

relations.definition: To make something clear or understandable by providing information or context.
relations.embedding_query_text: explains: To make something clear or understandable by providing information or context.

chosen_property.label: explains
chosen_property.definition: To make something clear or understandable by describing or interpreting it.
chosen_property.justification: No existing property fits the relation.

candidates.label: ratingExplanation
candidates.comment: A rating explanation relation between a rating and a brief text providing context or justification for the rating. Also called rating justification, explanation for rating, rating context. Examples: "A product rating includes a rating explanation 'The battery life was excellent, but the camera was disappointing'.", "A fact-check rating has a rating explanation 'The claim was partially true, lacking full context'.", "A service rating has a rating explanation 'The staff were friendly, but wait times were long'."

candidates.label: backstory
candidates.comment: A textual summary providing context and explanation for how and why an article was created. Also called: background story, context, origin story. Examples: "Article 'Investigative Report' backstory 'The journalist spent months...'", "NewsArticle 'Exposed Scandal' backstory 'This article originated from a tip-off...'."

candidates.label: originalMediaContextDescription
candidates.comment: Background information that aids in better interpretation of a media object, especially for decontextualized content in a media review. Also called media context, original context, background description. Examples: "Media Review A originalMediaContextDescription 'Video was originally posted on TikTok in 2020.'", "Image Review B originalMediaContextDescription 'Photo taken during a protest in 2018, not current event.'", "Audio Review C originalMediaContextDescription 'Clip is from a satirical podcast, not a news broadcast.'". Distinct from reviewBody, which is the main text of the review.

candidates.label: answerExplanation
candidates.comment: An answer explanation relation between an answer and a comment or web content providing a detailed clarification or step-by-step reasoning. Also called solution explanation, answer justification, detailed response. Examples: "An answer's answer explanation details the calculation steps.", "The correct answer's explanation clarifies the underlying principle."

candidates.label: knowsAbout
candidates.comment: A knowledge domain relation between an organization or person and a topic or entity they possess knowledge about. Also called knowledgeable about, familiar with topic, understands, has expertise in (without implying skill level). Examples: A person knowsAbout 'artificial intelligence'. An organization knowsAbout 'renewable energy policy'. A researcher knowsAbout 'quantum physics'. Distinct from hasOccupation or alumniOf, which are about formal roles or education, not general knowledge.

candidates.label: description
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation between a thing and its textual description. Also called: item description, details, explanation. Examples: "Product" description "A versatile smartphone with advanced camera features.", "Event" description "An annual conference for tech enthusiasts.", "Person" description "A renowned scientist and author.". Distinct from disambiguatingDescription, which is specifically for disambiguation.

candidates.label: disambiguatingDescription
candidates.comment: A clarifying description relation between a thing and a short text used to distinguish it from similar items. Also called: clarifying description, distinguishing text, unique description. Examples: "Apple" disambiguating description "The fruit, not the company.", "Mercury" disambiguating description "The planet, not the element.", "Jaguar" disambiguating description "The animal, not the car brand.". Distinct from description, which is a general description.

candidates.label: speakable
candidates.comment: A designation of sections within an article or webpage that are highlighted as particularly suitable for text-to-speech conversion. Also called "text-to-speech section", "audible content", "read-aloud section", "speech-optimized content". Examples: "The news article has speakable the main body text", "This webpage's speakable sections are identified by CSS selectors", "The speakable content is specified by a URL fragment."

candidates.label: temporal
candidates.comment: A general temporal relation between a creative work and a date or time, used when more specific temporal properties are not applicable. Also called "related to time", "time context", "associated temporal period", "timeframe". Examples: "The novel has temporal the 19th century", "The painting's temporal is the Renaissance era", "This document's temporal is the year 2020.". Distinct from temporalCoverage, which indicates the specific time period the content applies to.

candidates.label: softwareHelp
candidates.comment: A relation between a software application and a creative work providing assistance or guidance for its use. Also called "application help", "software documentation", "user guide for software". Examples: "Microsoft Word has softwareHelp a user manual", "The app's softwareHelp is an online FAQ", "This softwareHelp explains how to use the program."

chosen_property.label: actor
chosen_property.justification: Flipped to inverse to match the subject-object direction.

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: additionalNumberOfGuests
candidates.comment: An additional number of guests relation between an RSVP action and the count of extra attendees beyond the invitee. Also called plus-one count, extra guests, total additional attendees. Examples: "An RSVP action's additional number of guests is '2'.", "The wedding RSVP indicates an additional number of guests of '1'."

candidates.label: numAdults
candidates.comment: The number of adults included in a lodging reservation. Also called adult count, number of grown-ups, adult guests. Examples: "Hotel Reservation numAdults 2", "Vacation Rental numAdults 4", "Single Room Reservation numAdults 1". Distinct from numChildren, which specifies the number of children.

candidates.label: lodgingUnitType
candidates.comment: A unit type relation between a lodging reservation and the textual or qualitative description of the unit. Also called: room type, accommodation category, unit classification. Examples: "Hotel Reservation lodgingUnitType 'Suite'", "Motel Booking lodgingUnitType 'Double Room'", "Resort Reservation lodgingUnitType 'Villa'".

candidates.label: lodgingUnitDescription
candidates.comment: A unit description relation between a lodging reservation and a full textual description of the lodging unit. Also called: room description, accommodation details, unit features. Examples: "Hotel Reservation lodgingUnitDescription 'King-size bed, ocean view, balcony'", "Apartment Rental lodgingUnitDescription 'Two bedrooms, fully equipped kitchen, city view'", "Cabin Booking lodgingUnitDescription 'Rustic cabin, fireplace, lake access'".

candidates.label: numChildren
candidates.comment: The number of children included in a lodging reservation. Also called child count, number of kids, child guests. Examples: "Hotel Reservation numChildren 1", "Vacation Rental numChildren 3", "Family Suite Reservation numChildren 2". Distinct from numAdults, which specifies the number of adults.

candidates.label: passengerPriorityStatus
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the priority status assigned to a passenger for a flight reservation. Also called boarding priority, security status, passenger status. Examples: A flight reservation has a passenger priority status of 'FastTrack'. A flight reservation has a passenger priority status of 'Priority Boarding'. A flight reservation has a passenger priority status of 'Elite Member'.

candidates.label: numberOfPartialBathrooms
candidates.comment: The total number of half and quarter bathrooms in an accommodation or floor plan. Also called partial bathroom count, half baths, quarter baths. Examples: "Apartment A numberOfPartialBathrooms 1", "House B numberOfPartialBathrooms 2", "Hotel Room C numberOfPartialBathrooms 0". Distinct from numberOfFullBathrooms, which specifies full or three-quarter bathrooms. numberOfBathroomsTotal is the sum of all types.

candidates.label: reservationFor
candidates.comment: A reservation for relation between a reservation and the specific item or service being booked. Also called booked item, reserved item, subject of reservation. Examples: "A reservation is for 'Flight BA249'.", "A restaurant booking is for 'Dinner at The Fancy Bistro'.", "A hotel reservation is for 'Room 301'."

candidates.label: producer
candidates.comment: A creative role relation between a creative work and the person or organization responsible for its production. Also called production company, executive producer, creator, maker. Examples: A movie has a producer 'Steven Spielberg'. A music album has a producer 'Universal Music Group'. A TV series has a producer 'Shonda Rhimes'. Distinct from director, who is responsible for the creative vision.

candidates.label: productionCompany
candidates.comment: A production relation between a creative work (like a movie or series) and the organization responsible for its creation. Also called produced by, studio, made by, created by. Examples: "The movie 'Dune' was produced by Legendary Pictures.", "The TV series 'The Crown' was produced by Left Bank Pictures.", "The video game 'Cyberpunk 2077' was produced by CD Projekt Red."

candidates.label: produces
candidates.comment: An outcome relation between a service and the tangible thing it generates or provides. Also called generates, yields, creates, provides. Examples: A government service produces a 'passport'. A licensing service produces a 'permit'. A printing service produces 'documents'.

candidates.label: productionDate
candidates.comment: A production date relation between a product or vehicle and the specific date it was manufactured. Also called manufactured on, made on, creation date. Examples: "A 2023 Toyota Camry has a production date of 2022-11-15.", "A vintage car has a production date of 1965-03-01.", "A smartphone has a production date of 2024-01-20."

candidates.label: manufacturer
candidates.comment: A manufacturing relation between a product and the organization that produced it. Also called: produced by, made by, fabricated by. Examples: "Smartphone manufacturer Apple", "Automobile manufacturer Toyota", "Furniture manufacturer IKEA".

candidates.label: recordedIn
candidates.comment: A recording capture relation between an event and the creative work that captured all or part of it. Also called captured by, documented in, featured in. Examples: "A concert event was recorded in 'a live album'.", "A historical event was recorded in 'a documentary film'.", "A speech event was recorded in 'a news broadcast'.". Distinct from recordedAt, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: resultReview
candidates.comment: The specific review created as the outcome of a review action. Also called generated review, review outcome, produced review. Examples: `ReviewAction on Product` resultReview `Customer's Product Review`, `ReviewAction on Movie` resultReview `Critic's Movie Review`, `ReviewAction on Service` resultReview `User Service Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: resultComment
candidates.comment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: countryOfOrigin
candidates.comment: A provenance relation between a creative work or product and its country of origin. Also called: origin country, produced in, made in. Examples: "French Wine" country of origin "France", "Japanese Anime" country of origin "Japan", "German Car" country of origin "Germany", "Hollywood Movie" country of origin "United States". Distinct from countryOfAssembly, which specifies where the product was put together.

candidates.label: expressedIn
candidates.comment: An expressed in relation between a gene and the anatomical structure, system, or biological entity where its activity has been experimentally observed. Also called: gene activity location, observed in, found in. Examples: "Gene A" expressed in "Brain", "Gene B" expressed in "Liver", "Gene C" expressed in "Digestive System".

candidates.label: hostingOrganization
candidates.comment: A hosting organization relation between a member program or program membership and the organization that offers or manages it. Also called program provider, membership organization, host company. Examples: "A member program has a hosting organization 'Airline X'.", "The program membership is with a hosting organization.", "This program is hosted by a specific organization."

candidates.label: gameServer
candidates.comment: A game server relation between a video game and the server where it can be played. Also called: hosted on, playable server, game host. Examples: "Minecraft" game server "Hypixel Network", "World of Warcraft" game server "Frostmourne Realm", "Call of Duty" game server "Dedicated Server". Distinct from game, which is the game itself.

candidates.label: isStoreOn
candidates.comment: A platform hosting relation between an online store and the e-commerce marketplace where it operates. Also called hosted on, operates on, platform for, marketplace for. Examples: An online store isStoreOn 'Amazon'. A small business's online store isStoreOn 'Etsy'. A vendor's shop isStoreOn 'eBay'.

candidates.label: homeTeam
candidates.comment: A home team relation between a sports event and the team or person designated as the home participant. Also called host team, home side, local team. Examples: "A sports event has a home team 'Lions'.", "The match features a home team.", "This event's home team is a specific person."

candidates.label: organizer
candidates.comment: An organization or person responsible for organizing an event. Also called event planner, host, coordinator, promoter. Examples: "Conference X organizer 'Acme Events Inc.'", "Concert Y organizer 'Live Nation'", "Workshop Z organizer 'Jane Doe'". Distinct from performer, who participates in the event.

candidates.label: game
candidates.comment: A game relation between a game server and the video game that is hosted and played on it. Also called: hosted game, server game, game played. Examples: "Minecraft Server" game "Minecraft", "World of Warcraft Realm" game "World of Warcraft", "CS:GO Server" game "Counter-Strike: Global Offensive".

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: additionalNumberOfGuests
candidates.comment: An additional number of guests relation between an RSVP action and the count of extra attendees beyond the invitee. Also called plus-one count, extra guests, total additional attendees. Examples: "An RSVP action's additional number of guests is '2'.", "The wedding RSVP indicates an additional number of guests of '1'."

candidates.label: numAdults
candidates.comment: The number of adults included in a lodging reservation. Also called adult count, number of grown-ups, adult guests. Examples: "Hotel Reservation numAdults 2", "Vacation Rental numAdults 4", "Single Room Reservation numAdults 1". Distinct from numChildren, which specifies the number of children.

candidates.label: aircraft
candidates.comment: An aircraft relation between a flight and the specific type of vehicle used for air travel. Also called airplane type, plane model, flight vehicle. Examples: "A flight's aircraft is 'Boeing 747'.", "The flight uses an 'Airbus A320'."

candidates.label: broadcastFrequency
candidates.comment: A frequency used for over-the-air broadcasts for a broadcast channel or service. Also called: broadcast frequency, radio frequency, channel frequency. Examples: "BroadcastChannel 'FM Station' broadcastFrequency '87.9 FM'", "BroadcastService 'TV Channel' broadcastFrequency 'BroadcastFrequencySpecification 500 MHz'."

candidates.label: estimatedFlightDuration
candidates.comment: An estimated flight duration relation between a flight and the duration or text representing its approximate travel time. Also called "approximate flight time", "expected flight length", "scheduled flight duration". Examples: "Flight 'UA123' estimatedFlightDuration 'PT5H30M'", "Flight 'DL456' estimatedFlightDuration '6 hours'", "Flight 'LH789' estimatedFlightDuration 'PT10H'".

candidates.label: broadcastOfEvent
candidates.comment: An event that is being broadcast by a broadcast event. Also called: televised event, event broadcast. Examples: "BroadcastEvent 'Super Bowl Live' broadcastOfEvent 'Super Bowl LVIII'", "BroadcastEvent 'Concert Stream' broadcastOfEvent 'Live Music Concert'."

candidates.label: isLiveBroadcast
candidates.comment: A broadcast status relation indicating whether a broadcast event is being transmitted in real-time. Also called live stream, real-time broadcast, live transmission. Examples: A sports game broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A news report broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A recorded TV show broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'false'.

candidates.label: arrivalAirport
candidates.comment: An arrival airport relation between a flight and the airport where it concludes. Also called destination airport, landing airport, final airport. Examples: "A flight's arrival airport is 'LAX'.", "The flight's arrival airport is 'Heathrow Airport'."

candidates.label: providesBroadcastService
candidates.comment: A broadcast service provision relation between a broadcast channel and the specific broadcast service it offers. Also called channel offers, service on channel, carries service. Examples: "Channel 5 provides broadcast service 'News at 6'.", "BBC One provides broadcast service 'EastEnders'.", "A radio channel provides broadcast service 'Morning Show'."

candidates.label: publishedOn
candidates.comment: A broadcast publication relation between a publication event and the broadcast service on which it was published. Also called aired on, broadcast via, released on service. Examples: "A TV show's publication event was published on 'BBC One'.", "A radio program's publication event was published on 'NPR'.", "A news segment's publication event was published on 'CNN'."

candidates.label: inBroadcastLineup
candidates.comment: A broadcast lineup relation between a broadcast channel and the cable or satellite service that offers it. Also called offered by, part of lineup, channel provider. Examples: "A broadcast channel is in a broadcast lineup of 'CableCo'.", "The channel is part of a satellite service's lineup.", "This channel is offered by a specific broadcast lineup."

candidates.label: hasBroadcastChannel
candidates.comment: A channel association relation between a broadcast service and one of its broadcast channels. Also called includes channel, offers channel, channel of. Examples: "A TV service has a broadcast channel for news.", "A radio service has a broadcast channel for music.", "The streaming service has a broadcast channel for sports."

chosen_property.label: streams
chosen_property.definition: To transmit or receive data in a continuous flow over the internet.
chosen_property.justification: No existing property fits the relation.

candidates.label: isLiveBroadcast
candidates.comment: A broadcast status relation indicating whether a broadcast event is being transmitted in real-time. Also called live stream, real-time broadcast, live transmission. Examples: A sports game broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A news report broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A recorded TV show broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'false'.

candidates.label: broadcastOfEvent
candidates.comment: An event that is being broadcast by a broadcast event. Also called: televised event, event broadcast. Examples: "BroadcastEvent 'Super Bowl Live' broadcastOfEvent 'Super Bowl LVIII'", "BroadcastEvent 'Concert Stream' broadcastOfEvent 'Live Music Concert'."

candidates.label: embedUrl
candidates.comment: An embed URL relation between a media object and the URL pointing to a player for that media. Also called "player URL", "embed link", "streaming URL". Examples: "Video mediaObject embedUrl 'youtube.com/embed/videoid'", "Audio mediaObject embedUrl 'soundcloud.com/player/trackid'", "Interactive content embedUrl 'example.com/interactive/player'". Distinct from contentUrl, which is the direct URL to the media file itself.

candidates.label: bitrate
candidates.comment: A textual description of the bitrate of a media object. Also called: data rate, transfer rate, bandwidth. Examples: "MediaObject 'Video File' bitrate '10 Mbps'", "MediaObject 'Audio Stream' bitrate '320 kbps'."

candidates.label: hasBroadcastChannel
candidates.comment: A channel association relation between a broadcast service and one of its broadcast channels. Also called includes channel, offers channel, channel of. Examples: "A TV service has a broadcast channel for news.", "A radio service has a broadcast channel for music.", "The streaming service has a broadcast channel for sports."

candidates.label: tributary
candidates.comment: A tributary relation between a vein and the larger anatomical structure or organ system it flows into. Also called drains into, connects to, flows into. Examples: "Small saphenous vein tributary 'popliteal vein'", "Renal vein tributary 'inferior vena cava'", "Vein tributary 'larger vein'".

candidates.label: requiresSubscription
candidates.comment: A subscription requirement relation indicating whether an action access or media object necessitates a subscription for use. Also called subscription needed, paywall, access restriction. Examples: "A streaming movie requires subscription 'true'.", "A news article requires subscription 'false'.", "A premium feature requires subscription 'true'."

candidates.label: regionsAllowed
candidates.comment: A regions allowed relation between a media object and the geographical areas where its use is permitted. Also called allowed in, permitted regions, geographical availability. Examples: "A movie streaming service has regions allowed 'US, Canada'.", "A music video has regions allowed 'Europe'.", "A software download has regions allowed 'Worldwide'."

candidates.label: drainsTo
candidates.comment: A drainage relation between a vein and the vessel it empties into. Also called "empties into", "flows into", "tributary to". Examples: "Great saphenous vein drainsTo 'Femoral vein'", "Internal jugular vein drainsTo 'Subclavian vein'", "Renal vein drainsTo 'Inferior vena cava'".

candidates.label: broadcastSubChannel
candidates.comment: A subchannel identification for a broadcast frequency specification. Also called "subchannel of broadcast", "broadcast channel identifier". Examples: "FM 98.1 specification broadcastSubChannel 'HD2'", "Digital TV channel 5 specification broadcastSubChannel '5.3'".
